patches.reason: Settings the rules menu turns off and saves come back on at the next start: they are read as loadBoolean(key) ?: true, and Groovy elvis treats a saved false like a missing value. Read the saved value, and take true only where nothing is saved.

The computer chose its shot by placing the player's unsunk ships at random 10,000 times by default, retrying each placement until it fits the shots so far, without a wait; the legacy player computed that in about a third of a second on an empty board. A TeaseScript run stops a session after 1,000,000 steps without a wait (TSR037), and one such think takes about 14 times that, more once ships are hit, so the first enemy turn stopped the package. The think rests for a hundredth of a second every 1,000 placements, which lets the player run it in parts; the configured tries, the placement and shot-selection algorithms, and the existing time-based shortening stay as they were. The rests add about 0.9 seconds on an empty board, more where placements need retries; since they count toward the elapsed time, a short time limit can end the think earlier. The owner kept the legacy strength (decision 2026-10-10); a runtime that runs a long computation in parts is the real fix (#827).
